text:
Maya: FYI seeing p99 spikes on chat-prod around 10:12 UTC. Autoscaler decisions didn't help; warm pool reported 0 in us-west-2. KV-cache evictions climbed. tagging @Alex @Jorge @Sophie
Infra-bot: ALERT: inference.p99 > 1500ms (10:12:07)  Created INC-2026-310, paging oncall-sre.
Alex: Oncall ack. I'll start digging into infra and autoscaler logs.
Jorge: Runtime notes: kernel-selector fell back to generic CUDA kernels for a subset of requests (small batch + long context). Fallback increases per-token latency ~3x-4x.
Sophie: KV cache churn visible: kv_cache_evictions spiked on multiple shards, correlates with the latency window. Multi-turn chats are evicting prefixes.
Kevin: Autoscaler metrics I pulled: scale_up_cooldown=30s. But instance_provision_time median jumped to ~70s during the spike. Warm pool min=0 so new instances were cold.
Maya: Any noisy-neighbor signals on the nodes that first accepted traffic?
Jorge: Yes host_io_wait and docker_image_pull spikes on two hosts. One host was running a background compile job (batcher compiler). Likely noisy neighbour.
Sophie: Batching heuristics also harmed us: traffic pattern created many tiny batches that got routed to newly provisioned nodes with empty KV cache. Tiny batches + generic kernel = bad P99.
Kevin: Prometheus query I ran:

  # avg provision time (5m)
  sum(rate(instance_provision_time_seconds_sum[5m])) / sum(rate(instance_provision_time_seconds_count[5m]))

jumped from ~18s -> ~70s in the incident window.
Maya: Short-term mitigations proposal:
- bump warm_pool_min to 1 per AZ for chat-prod
- enable prewarm_image=true for the autoscaler policy
- temporarily pin top chat tenants to dedicated pool
- add guard in kernel-selector to avoid generic fallback for seq_len>256 + batch_size>=2
Thoughts?
Jorge: I can push a low-risk guard to kernel-selector quickly. It will prefer optimized fused kernels when context>256 and batch_size>=2. I'll attach nvprof traces to the infra channel.
Kevin: I'll update autoscaler policy: set warm_pool_min=1, prewarm_image=true, and diversify instance types in the pool to reduce co-location risk. Will canary a small change.
Deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for autoscaler-config (canary=15%, id: deploy-2143).
Profiler-bot: Uploaded profiler snapshots (nvprof and CUPTI) for the 10:12 window to /var/artifacts/INC-2026-310/traces.tar.gz.
Alex: After canary, instance_provision_time dropped back to ~22s. Monitoring p99 and kv evictions.
Sophie: Observed p99 drop from ~1850ms -> ~430ms in 10m after mitigations. KV evictions down ~60%.
Jorge: Bisected kernel selector issue; root cause is a dtype/shape handling change from the recent quantization patch. That produced an unexpected dtype combo and pushed fallback path. Will roll a fix and a unit test.
Kevin: Full rollout of autoscaler config complete. Added a temporary override in infra playbook to prefer warm instances for chat-prod.
Maya: Marking this incident in progress -> resolving once stable. @Jorge please post kernel-selection traces and PR link. @Sophie keep kv_eviction alerting on for 24h.
Jorge: Traces and write-up uploaded to /internal/eng-runtime/incidents/INC-2026-310. PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/981 (fix + test).
Maya: Incident marked resolved once metrics stabilized. Filing postmortem PM-2026-42. Thanks all. :heavy_check_mark:
Infra-bot: Incident INC-2026-310 status: RESOLVED (10:23:54). Postmortem ticket PM-2026-42 created.
